editorial:
Set in ancient Han Imperial China, this animated adventure follows an enslaved girl named Ping who stumbles onto one of the last dragon eggs after dragons were banished from the kingdom. When palace guards force her to run, she teams up with an old dragon named Long Danzi to return the egg to the ocean and save dragons from extinction. Ping soon discovers she is a true Dragonkeeper. The whole thing feels like a warm, old-school fantasy with a big heart, and Ping is the kind of brave, scrappy hero kids and adults can both root for.

The animation is colorful and lively, the action keeps moving, and the bond between Ping and Long Danzi gives the story real emotional weight. It can feel a little rushed in spots and some side characters are thin, but the pacing mostly works and the finale lands well. If you enjoy family fantasy with dragons, this is an easy pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ping fully accepts her role as a true Dragonkeeper and helps Long Danzi reach the ocean with the egg. The egg hatches, bringing new life to the dragon species and proving dragons can return to the world. The palace guards are stopped, and Ping is freed from slavery, stepping into a new future as protector of the dragons.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated fantasy adventures and dragon stories.
